question: A 6-day-old infant who was born via uncomplicated vaginal delivery at 39 weeks of gestation is brought to the family physician for poor feeding. The mother received adequate prenatal care throughout the pregnancy, and has no medical conditions. On physical exam, the infant's temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F), blood pressure is 70/45 mmHg, pulse is 170/min, and respirations are 40/min. The infant has dry mucous membranes, capillary refill of 4 seconds, and a depressed anterior fontanelle. No abdominal masses are noted. Genital exam shows enlargement of the clitoris with fusion of the labioscrotal folds. Serum chemistry is remarkable for hyponatremia and hyperkalemia. The infant's karyotype is 46,XX. Which of the following findings are most likely to be discovered upon further workup?

options.opd: Increased sex hormones, decreased renin activity

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Enlargement of the clitoris with fusion of the labioscrotal folds" -> "46,XX karyotype" -> "Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) suspected" -> 80% CHAIN: "Hyponatremia, hyperkalemia" -> "Decreased aldosterone" -> "Increased 11-deoxycorticosterone" -> 70% CHAIN: "Depressed anterior fontanelle" -> "Dehydration" -> "Increased 17-hydroxyprogesterone" -> 60% CHAIN: "Poor feeding" -> "Possible salt-wasting crisis" -> "Increased sex hormones, increased 17-hydroxyprogesterone" -> 80%
analysis: The infant is presenting with signs and symptoms suggestive of congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH), specifically 21-hydroxylase deficiency. This condition leads to decreased cortisol production, resulting in increased ACTH stimulation of the adrenal cortex and subsequent overproduction of adrenal androgens. The 46,XX karyotype with ambiguous genitalia (enlarged clitoris, fusion of labioscrotal folds) is consistent with the diagnosis. The electrolyte abnormalities (hyponatremia, hyperkalemia) are due to aldosterone deficiency. Therefore, the most likely finding upon further workup would be increased sex hormones and increased 17-hydroxyprogesterone due to the enzyme deficiency in the steroidogenesis pathway.
